newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Cotton - India, Pakistan prices seen subdued.
newsitem.headline: Cotton - India, Pakistan prices seen subdued.

text.p: Cotton prices in India and Pakistan are likely to remain subdued next week amid slack demand from mills, dealers said on Friday.
In Pakistan, rates closed steady in lacklustre trading on Wednesday before the market began a four-day break for the Moslem Eid al-Adha festival.

Nasim Usman, a broker at the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA), said prices were likely to open unchanged on Monday on slow mill demand, with unsold stocks at ginneries of more than a million 375-lb bales overhanging the market.
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 variety was quoted at 2,100/2,225 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), K-68 at 2,450/2,475 and MNH-93 at 2,460/2,485.

In India, cotton prices fell this week on sluggish mill demand and improved supply after transport operators ended their strike on April 10, traders said.
The 10-day strike, called to protest against a five percent service charge and a steep hike in insurance premiums, had crippled the supply of cotton across the country.
Average daily arrivals in India's northern state of Punjab rose to 10,000/12,000 bales from 4,000/5,000 bales in the first two weeks of the month.
"Mill demand is low and export business is dull and I am expecting local prices to remain subdued or move in a narrow price band in the coming days," said Chandulal Thakker, a leading cotton trader.

In spot, Bengal-deshi fell 25 rupees to 880/925 rupees per maund and Punjab saw-ginned lost 20/40 rupees to 1,510/1,640. Gujarat Kalyan (medium staple) shed 500 rupees to 13,200/13,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg). Long-staple Gujarat Sankar-4 lost 400/500 rupees to 15,500/17,000 rupees per candy for the average variety and to 18,000/19,300 rupees for the superior variety.
